scope: Research only: reopen native09 observations, production IosSnapshotFileSystem and L08 observer; inspect installed SDK declarations, authoritative Apple documentation and applicable upstream implementation. No production/control edits, builds, tests, native probes, simulator actions, process attachments, or other-task cleanup.
summary: Actual09 proves that the required directory NSFileManager attribute getter returned a dictionary without NSFileProtectionKey, without NSError. The file getter was diagnostic-only and showed the same absence. Both independent volume capability queries returned supported.

Public swift-foundation source at immutable commit 60bd7a1d8a730ebdeab2cb037b0519ef3b010ed3 explicitly excludes Simulator from the FileManager protection getter/setter path. Surrounding attribute-population helpers do not add this key. This supplies authoritative implementation counter-evidence to an application bug or unsupported-volume inference.

The inspected tag is not attested as the exact Foundation binary loaded by the iOS26.5/23F77 Simulator. The protected NSData open/relocation implementation also delegates to non-public Foundation helpers. Therefore exact installed-runtime behavior and physical Data Protection remain unverified.

Do not weaken the original L08 equality assertions, reinterpret the failed run as PASS, change entitlements, or change production storage on this evidence alone. A tiny separately-owned native Foundation control can distinguish current Simulator/API behavior from Kotlin/application handling.

authoritative_references.claim: NSFileProtectionKey identifies file protection level; value is NSString. No Simulator-specific guarantee is documented here.
authoritative_references.applicability: The exact key imported by production and probe; installed SDK declares iOS4+ availability.

authoritative_references.claim: Complete requests encrypted storage accessible only while unlocked. SDK defines Atomic=1 and Complete=0x20000000, so production bitwise OR is not an evident option-combination error.
authoritative_references.applicability: API/constant contract, not physical or Simulator execution proof.

authoritative_references.claim: Boolean capability of the containing volume, not the protection class of an individual item. NSURL.h310–313 permits a volume-key query via either file or directory URL.
authoritative_references.applicability: Explains why supported is not inconsistent with a Foundation getter that omits per-file metadata; does not establish actual protection.

authoritative_references.claim: Directory creation accepts attributes for newly created directories; not a guaranteed repair of an already-existing directory.
authoritative_references.applicability: Production lazy base path uses createIntermediates=true; actual09 does not independently measure first creation.

authoritative_references.claim: Official prose includes ignored attribute rejections and a limited parameter list; cannot infer protection behavior from missing list entries. SDK return-value comments alone also cannot prove every attribute persisted.
authoritative_references.applicability: Counter-evidence to relying only on create/set success; reinforces measured readback, not a recommendation to weaken it.

authoritative_references.claim: Xcode26.5 includes Swift6.3 and iOS26.5 SDK and supports macOS26.2+. Entire primary release-note content examined; no File Protection issue found.
authoritative_references.applicability: Exact locally installed Xcode/SDK family; lack of a release-note entry is not proof of support.

authoritative_references.claim: The getter populates protectionKey only inside !targetEnvironment(simulator) && FOUNDATION_FRAMEWORK. FileManager setter990–1000 has the same exclusion. stat attribute population164–201 and Utilities86–124 catInfo do not add protectionKey; extended attributes remain nested. Bridge46–71 forwards to this implementation.
authoritative_references.applicability: Immutable official Swift project implementation source, not a forum or swift-corelibs Linux substitute; exact installed Foundation image/source correspondence remains unestablished.

authoritative_references.claim: Darwin/Foundation recursive directory creation returns immediately for EEXIST and applies attributes to new directories through try? setAttributes; comment explicitly preserves binary compatibility.
authoritative_references.applicability: Shows why source-level attribute request/create success does not itself establish persisted class in this implementation. Does not prove this was the native09 creation path.

authoritative_references.claim: Foundation Data writing delegates to private _NSOpenFileDescriptor_Protected; relocated atomic writes also delegate option computation to private _NSDataWritingOptionsForRelocatedAtomicWrite. Public source alone does not reveal whether those helpers suppress/apply Complete for this Simulator.
authoritative_references.applicability: Preserves a critical limit: FileManager getter omission is not proof that NSData wrote plaintext or no per-file protection.

authoritative_references.claim: OS Foundation includes swift-foundation source; swift-corelibs-foundation is non-Darwin only and best-effort compatibility.
authoritative_references.applicability: Makes source family relevant but is not a binary provenance guarantee for a particular OS image.

authoritative_references.claim: Apple-silicon Macs support Data Protection and developers can opt into higher per-file/per-extent classes. macOS26.4 default FileVault statement does not apply to this26.2 host.
authoritative_references.applicability: Counter-evidence to a blanket claim that a Mac host cannot support File Protection. Previously retained primary visible paragraphs reopened; fresh body attempt exceeded300KB bound and is not used as new proof.

authoritative_references.claim: Current Apple guidance says simulated devices do not replicate every physical-device feature and physical testing remains needed.
authoritative_references.applicability: General boundary only; current page includes newer Device Hub terminology and does not specify File Protection behavior for26.5.

authoritative_references.claim: Archive is retired/deprecated for Xcode9+ (2018); examined visible text does not specify current File Protection behavior.
authoritative_references.applicability: Historical lead only, not proof of either current support or unsupported status.

smallest_next_fixture_proposal.purpose: On the exact owned Debug app-host and iOS26.5/23F77 runtime, independently measure native Foundation creation/write/readback without Koin/session/Keychain/Kotlin mapping. Do not start a new runner architecture.
ownership: Use root-owned single native lane after secondary FIFO ownership cleanup is resolved. Fresh task-owned simulator only; no connected phone or existing user profile.

Use a fresh token-bound Application Support child outside Parlor/snapshots and all production/legacy/rejoin names. Attest app bundle/UDID/container/parent and exact file types; reject symlinks/existing destination. No real player data or keychain access.

Keep only1 directory and1 small public fixed-ASCII fixture file for primary control; optional different files only if the primary result warrants them. Bound names, bytes, retries, receipts, and cleanup.
smallest_next_fixture_proposal.native_boundary: Prefer direct Objective-C NSFileManager/NSData selectors (or a reviewed Swift bridge that demonstrably calls those same Objective-C APIs), so Kotlin map/string bridging is removed without silently replacing NSData with an unrelated writer.
primary_steps: Create the fresh directory using attributes NSFileProtectionKey:NSFileProtectionComplete and createIntermediates=true. Record Boolean/typed NSError category+code; immediately read directory NSFileManager attributes.

Apply native URL backup exclusion only to this fixture directory and read attributes again to distinguish creation versus subsequent attribute handling; never apply a protection repair to a production directory.

Write the small fixture via NSData options Atomic|FileProtectionComplete. Record return/error; read native NSFileManager protection and, for this regular file only, fresh NSURLFileProtectionKey using the corresponding NSURL protection constants.
Apply fixture file backup exclusion and repeat these bounded metadata observations. Query volume support separately using fresh URLs; do not substitute the capability Boolean for per-item Complete.

Record only closed metadata enums/booleans/error category+code plus approved source/runtime/image identity. Do not record raw paths, complete dictionaries, payload, NSError descriptions, credentials, or private state.

Always collect compact receipt and execute owner-attested exact cleanup of fixture entries, app/test workers, DerivedData and generated build outputs; stop Gradle immediately and again after cleanup as required.
optional_followups: If needed, compare a second non-atomic Complete file and a third explicit native setAttributes file, preserving each pre/post observation; do not mutate the primary control into a success.
If native Foundation differs from Kotlin, read the same owned synthetic file from both with documented key types and bind observations to one process/run.

If native NSFileManager omits the key but NSURL returns Complete, investigate getter-surface differences; this still does not prove hardware lock/backup semantics. No private APIs/entitlement changes.
interpretation: Native getter also omits protection after the same direct calls: current runtime reproduction independent of Parlor/Kotlin; consistent with identified upstream Simulator guard. It does not prove universal Simulator incapability or absence of underlying encryption.

Native getter reports Complete but Parlor does not: current upstream equivalence assumption is insufficient; compare creation timing, backup attribute application, Objective-C bridge and exact types/paths without changing production first.
Any native creation/write/query error is a distinct controlled observation, not proof that original application code is wrong.

Original L08 gate remains failed/unresolved until its applicability is deliberately classified on this evidence. A control witness is not repair evidence and does not execute the original missing storage boots. Physical lock/unlock, backup and Store-qualified signing remain separate.
